description: “I’m Advik from Grade 4C! I coded Astro Tether in Scratch. Keep your astronaut alive in space by collecting oxygen and food, and fight the robot boss with lasers!”
summary: I made a Scratch game called Astro Tether. An astronaut is floating in space, and his oxygen keeps running out. The player moves him with the W, A, S and D keys to collect oxygen tanks and space food, which give back oxygen and points. After about two minutes, a giant robot boss arrives and fires lasers. The player presses 1 to shoot back, and every shot uses oxygen. If oxygen runs out, the game is over. My game shows how important oxygen and food are for astronauts’ survival in space.
details:
What does it do / how does it work?
It’s a space survival game. The astronaut’s oxygen goes down by 2 every 2 seconds. Collecting an oxygen tank gives +5 oxygen and +10 points. Space food appears for a short time and gives +15 oxygen and +30 points. Later, a boss robot arrives with lasers. Touching the boss or its lasers costs oxygen. At 0 oxygen, the game shows “out of oxygen game over”.

What benefits does it have?
It teaches that astronauts need oxygen and food to survive. It also builds quick thinking, planning and hand–eye coordination.

What is the intended impact?
I want players to understand the dangers astronauts face and to get excited about space and coding.

What tools did you use?
I used Scratch 3 (block coding) on a computer. I used:

  • Variables for oxygen, score and boss HP
  • Broadcasts to start the game
  • Clones for the lasers
  • Timers and random numbers so items appear in different places
  • Sensing blocks to check when the astronaut touches things

How is it creative?
I combined a survival game with a boss battle. Firing a laser costs oxygen, so the player has to decide when to attack and when to save oxygen. I also used real astronaut equipment, like oxygen tanks and space food.

What factors did I consider?

  • Balance: Oxygen must drop fast enough to be exciting but not too fast.
  • Random items: Items appear in random places, so every game is different.
  • Challenge: The boss arrives later, so the game gets harder over time.
  • Clear feedback: The oxygen, score and boss HP are always shown on screen.
